points.label: Feature focus timeline: tap to choose which curves are active
points.summary: The timeline's legend is now the curve PICKER. On a phone, open /pulse/timeline.html and scroll to the 'Curves' block under the chart. PASS = (1) the chips are comfortable thumb targets, not 30px slivers, and the header reads '6 of 25 shown'; (2) a single tap on any subject adds or removes its curve immediately, and the chip's mark flips ○ ↔ ✓; (3) pressing and HOLDING a chip for about half a second leaves only that subject on the chart and the header changes to 'only <subject>' — holding it again brings your previous set back; (4) tapping a curve directly in the chart does the same isolation, while dragging the chart to pan changes nothing about which curves are shown; (5) after panning/zooming the chart, the chips are still immediately tappable (they used to be re-drawn mid-gesture); (6) reload the page — it opens on the curves you picked, not back on the default six. FAIL = any tap that needs a second attempt, a hold that toggles the curve back off when you lift your finger, a drag that silently changes the selection, or a selection lost on reload. Please note which phone/browser, since the hold gesture takes a different code path on iOS (timer) than on Android (contextmenu).

actions.text: Verified in headless Chromium at 390x844 with touch (tests/e2e/pulse-timeline.spec.js, 8 cases). This request is the real-device confirmation of the two gestures a simulator cannot prove: the ~500ms hold, and whether the 44px chips actually feel tappable in the hand.
